title: fix: prevent message actions from repeating bot responses
body:
<!-- Please provide the issue number here if any -->

> Fixes #5849

## Changelog Entry

<!-- Please paste your new entry from CHANGELOG.MD here. Entry is not required for work only related to development purposes. -->

- Fixed screen readers repeating the full bot response when focus enters message actions such as Copy, Like, or Dislike, resolving [#5849](https://github.com/microsoft/BotFramework-WebChat/issues/5849), by [@asalsa](https://github.com/asalsa)

## Description

<!-- Please discuss the changes you have worked on. What do the changes do; why is this PR needed? -->

Windows Narrator repeats an entire bot response when keyboard focus first enters native message actions such as Copy, Like, or Dislike. The controls already expose concise accessible names, so adding another button label does not break the relationship that causes the repeated response.

Latest-main source still labeled the role-less outer stacked-layout container with the inner message row. The label target contains the greeting, full response, and action toolbar. A live accessibility-tree reproduction using published `botframework-webchat@4.19.1`, which contains the same relationship, showed that the actions had concise names while an ancestor accessible name contained the full response. This explains why the Agent Builder article-level workaround does not resolve the nested Web Chat context announced when focus enters an action.

This change removes the redundant accessible-name relationship from the outer layout and removes its now-unused generated ID. The inner message group and transcript article continue to expose message context and navigation semantics.

Reproduction:

1. Render a long bot response with `AllowCopy`, `LikeAction`, and `DislikeAction`.
2. Set `feedbackActionsPlacement` to `activity-actions`.
3. Start Narrator in Edge.
4. Move focus into Copy, Like, or Dislike.
5. Before this change, Narrator announces the full response as ancestor context before the concise action name.
6. After this change, the action no longer has an ancestor accessible name derived from the response.

Manual Edge plus Narrator validation passed for the #5849 first-focus announcement: keyboard-driven focus on Copy announced only “Copy, button,” and arrow navigation announced Like and Dislike without repeating the response. A separate transcript activation regression remains: activating the blue-outlined transcript activity reports “Item has no primary action” instead of moving focus into the message actions.

## Design

<!-- If this feature is complicated in nature, please provide additional clarifications. -->

The fix breaks the proven causal relationship instead of changing button labels, moving the toolbar, or modifying the activity article. It does not change localization, DOM order, keyboard order, or focus order. The message row remains `role="group"` with `aria-roledescription="message"`, and transcript navigation remains represented by its `article` active descendant.

`StackedLayoutRoot` has two callers. The part-grouping caller never supplied the removed label prop, and the message-layout caller was its only user. The generated message-row ID had no remaining caller after removing the outer relationship.

## Specific Changes

<!-- Please list the changes in a concise manner. -->

- Removed `aria-labelledby` from the role-less stacked-layout container.
- Removed the generated ID and prop wiring used only by that relationship.
- Added an HTML integration regression with native Copy, Like, and Dislike.
- Asserted computed AX action names, absence of response-derived ancestor AX names, message grouping, and transcript article navigation.
- Added a test-harness RPC for Selenium's result-returning DevTools command.
- Updated `CHANGELOG.md`.

Validation:

- Passed `npm clean-install --userconfig .npmrc`.
- Passed `npm run build-browser` on Windows.
- Passed full `npm run build` for the PR commit in an isolated Linux container. The archive's CRLF shell scripts were normalized only inside the disposable validation volume.
- Passed `npm test -- --testPathPattern "__tests__/html2/accessibility/messageActions\.html$"` in the documented Selenium Grid through the Linux validation container: 1 suite and 1 test passed.
- Passed `.\node_modules\.bin\eslint.cmd --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0 packages\component\src packages\test\harness\src`.
- Passed `npm run precommit:typecheck --workspace ./packages/component`.
- Passed `npm exec prettier -- --check` for every changed component, HTML test, and harness file.
- Passed `git diff --check`.
- Reconfirmed live Chrome AX causal evidence against published `botframework-webchat@4.19.1`, not the PR build: action names were `Copy`, `Like`, and `Dislike`; the response-bearing ancestor name existed before removing the outer relationship and disappeared afterward; the message group and transcript article remained.
- Windows Jest discovery remains environment-specific in this worktree because its resolved glob contains `BotFramework-WebChat\.worktrees`; the same focused test passed through the Linux Selenium Grid route.
- Passed manual Edge plus Narrator first-focus validation using a keyboard-only helper that moved DOM focus into Copy. Narrator announced Copy, Like, and Dislike without repeating the bot response.
- Observed separately: while the transcript activity has the blue active-descendant outline, Narrator reports “Item has no primary action” and does not move focus into the controls. The repository contract says Enter should work with or without scan mode, but this PR does not change `BasicTranscript`, `ActivityRow`, or `FocusTrap`.
- GitHub pull-request validation remains `action_required` with zero jobs until a maintainer authorizes the workflow.

<!-- For bugs, add the bug repro as a test. Otherwise, add tests to futureproof your work. -->

- [x] I have added tests and executed them locally
- [x] I have updated `CHANGELOG.md`
- [ ] I have updated documentation

## Review Checklist

- [ ] Browser and platform compatibilities reviewed
- [ ] CSS styles reviewed (minimal rules, no `z-index`)

- [ ] `package.json` and `package-lock.json` reviewed
- [ ] Security reviewed (no data URIs, check for nonce leak)
- [ ] Tests reviewed (coverage, legitimacy)
